children: The Indian payments landscape is bracing for significant instability as the Reserve Bank of India’s September 15 deadline for Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance looms, according to payment industry executives.
Industry estimates suggest approximately 30-35 percent of small-scale offline merchants deploying QR codes for UPI payments may fail to meet the regulatory timeline.
Additionally, a million small online business entities are at risk of missing the verification window.
This stringent compliance mandate encompasses all merchant categories, including online, offline, and cross-border service providers.
Paytm, PhonePe and Google Pay did not respond to Moneycontrol queries on the quantum of backlog or how they plan to complete the re-KYC for millions of merchants before the RBI’s deadline.
RBI also did not offer any comments about the potential payment disruption. Most payment aggregators also did not respond to Moneycontrol's request for comments.

The KYC backlog follows the RBI’s updated and consolidated Master Directions, issued in September 2025, which formally categorise payment aggregators into three segments: PA-Online, PA-Physical and PA-Cross Border.

The central bank also set a September 15, 2026 deadline for payment aggregators to complete full re-KYC verification of existing merchants, failing which their payments will be paused. For merchants onboarded on or after January 1, 2026, verification was required before they could accept payments.

This impacts the long-tail of informal merchants in the online and offline world, who do not have proper documents as required by RBI. Most of these are individual-owned and run shops or businesses that do not understand the detailed documentation requirements.

“While RBI’s idea is to bring standardisation in the KYC norms, most mom-and-pop stores or kirana shops do not have the kind of documents needed to complete the verification,” said a senior executive with a payments firm.

According to sources, around 85-90 percent of the merchants using soundbox machines for UPI payments are likely to complete the KYC verification, while the smaller ones using QR code standees are more likely to comply with the deadline.

These merchants do not contribute much to the total payments volume or value and are unlikely to face any ecosystem-level impact in terms of volume or value. Most payment aggregators are likely to finish around 80 percent of the re-KYC by the deadline.

Many payment players are facing capacity constraints as RBI rules require in-person KYC to be done by the employees of the payment aggregator rather than a third-party agency. This required most players working with the long-tail informal merchant to hire additional staff over the last year.

“This is a non-trivial matter and required companies like PhonePe, Paytm and Google Pay to hire thousands of such employees across the country, including tier 3 towns and rural areas, unlike online payments players like Razorpay or Cashfree, which are rather in a more comfortable place,” said the CEO and founder of a payments firm.
Moneycontrol reported earlier that thousands of Google Play developers are struggling to complete their KYC before the RBI deadline.

title: Millions of small merchants face payment disruption as RBI’s re-KYC deadline nears
